text:
Predicates:
CanRegisterToVote(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateInElection(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
HasUSCitizenship(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina

Premises:
∀x (CanRegisterToVote(x) → ParticipateInElection(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
HasUSCitizenship(x) → CanRegisterToVote(x) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (HasUSCitizenship(x) ∨ HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (RussianOfficial(x) ∧ HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Vladimir)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegisterToVote(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.

Conclusion:
CanParticipateInElection(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Vladimir) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election or Vladimir is a manager at Gazprom.
